title: Secretless Deployment with Workload Identity
description: Authenticate pipelines to Azure with federated credentials so there is no client secret to rotate.

data.text: Your release pipeline authenticates to Azure with a service principal client secret stored as a pipeline variable. The secret expires in 12 months, is copied into three other pipelines, and one copy leaked into a build log. Redesign authentication so compromising the pipeline history gives an attacker no credential to reuse.

Replace the client secret with a **workload identity federation** (OpenID Connect) trust between your CI provider and a **user-assigned managed identity** or app registration in Microsoft Entra ID. The pipeline requests a short-lived OIDC token that Azure validates against the federated credential's subject claim. No secret is stored anywhere and nothing needs rotation.

data.title: Create the federated credential
data.code:
# Create a user-assigned managed identity for deployments
az identity create --name id-quotient-deploy --resource-group rg-platform

CLIENT_ID=$(az identity show --name id-quotient-deploy -g rg-platform --query clientId -o tsv)
PRINCIPAL_ID=$(az identity show --name id-quotient-deploy -g rg-platform --query principalId -o tsv)

# Grant it Contributor on the target resource group only
az role assignment create --assignee $PRINCIPAL_ID \
  --role Contributor --scope /subscriptions/$SUB/resourceGroups/rg-quotient-prod

# Trust GitHub Actions on the main branch of a specific repo
az identity federated-credential create \
  --name github-main \
  --identity-name id-quotient-deploy \
  --resource-group rg-platform \
  --issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --subject repo:my-org/quotient:ref:refs/heads/main \
  --audiences api://AzureADTokenExchange

data.title: GitHub Actions workflow using OIDC
data.code:
permissions:
  id-token: write      # required to request the OIDC token
  contents: read

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      - run: az webapp deploy --name app-quotient-prod -g rg-quotient-prod --src-path app.zip

data.text: A client secret is a bearer credential: anyone who reads it can use it from anywhere until it expires. An OIDC token is bound to a specific **issuer, repository, and branch**, valid for minutes, and cannot be replayed outside that context. Leaked pipeline logs become worthless to an attacker.

cards.title: Workload identity federation (OIDC)
cards.description: Short-lived token bound to repo and branch
pros: Works with GitHub, Azure DevOps, GitLab
cons: Must configure federated credential per repo/branch

cards.title: Service principal with client secret
cons: Secret must be stored and rotated

cards.title: Managed identity on a self-hosted runner
cons: Identity is shared across all jobs on the runner
